newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian shares eye U.S. for further direction.
newsitem.headline: Belgian shares eye U.S. for further direction.

text.p: Belgian shares ended with modest gains on Tuesday after swinging into the black in the afternoon following news of a slightly lower-than-expected rise in U.S. labour cost data for the fourth quarter.
The Bel-20 index .BFX finished 6.45 points or 0.32 percent higher at 2,050.44 after dipping to 2,029.55 before the figures.

"The dollar is at good levels for European companies - and as long as this rally on Wall Street continues, we'll benefit," one dealer said. The U.S. data, which made a possible Fed rate rise seem less likely than had been thought before, were welcomed by bonds markets and then by Wall Street.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average .DJI stood 89 points or 1.4 percent higher at 6,751 in late afternoon in Europe.

One of the most heavily traded Belgian shares in value terms was oil major PetroFina, which said after the market closed that it expected its full-year 1996 net profit to rise 38 percent to 16.0 billion Belgian francs.
Sandra Vandersmissen, analyst at Generale Bank, said PetroFina's preliminary results were at the top end of the range of expectations and that the company's shares should benefit.
"I think everyone will have to raise their (1996) forecasts," she added.
Petrofina closed 50 francs higher at 11,350 before the news, with 17,059 shares traded.
U.S.-exposed retailer Delhaize was the most heavily traded, rising 0.3 percent to 1,925 francs on 123,937 shares.
Steel cord and wire maker Bekaert continued to benefit from bargain hunters which have been attracted back to the stock since mid-January, and rose 400 francs to 19,475.
Bekaert, which suffered last year from a company profits warning, dropped from 26,450 francs to 18,150 between late November and mid-December. It recovered slightly before easing to 18,525 last week.
